title: A Oath for the Hollow
premise: Kestrel Iversen flees his valley, where magic cannot follow, only to learn the crown's witch-hunt has already reached its borders. Hunted by a former friend turned inquisitor, he joins a ragged band of gifted fugitives seeking the Hollow Door, the last exit from a country whose name is being erased from maps, memory, and reality itself. To open the Door, someone must surrender their gift and their identity to the land that no longer exists. In the end, Kestrel pays that price, becoming the Door itself and letting the others pass into freedom, remembered by no one but the land he saved.
about_author: Rafael Reyes is a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping disappearing villages before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about borders, exile, and the people history forgets to name.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel tends his dying mentor's garden and hides the flicker of magic he was told would never follow him here — until it does. A crown writ nailed to the chapel door announces the hunt. He runs at dawn, grief and terror tangled. Emotional beat: the shattering of the only safety he has ever known.

chapters.title: Ash on the Toll Road
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. On the road he finds a burned waystation and a survivor, Sable, a gifted smuggler who saves him from a checkpoint sweep by lying brilliantly. She warns him the hunt is led by Inquisitor Dain — Kestrel's childhood friend. Emotional beat: wary alliance born of mutual desperation.

chapters.title: What the Maps No Longer Hold
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable reveals the rumor: the Hollow Door, an exit from the country the crown is unmaking. Kestrel's magic resonates with old boundary stones, proving he can find it. Dain's riders burn a village behind them. Emotional beat: hope kindled, then immediately shadowed by the cost of being found useful.

chapters.title: The Company of the Unwritten
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The fugitives gather in a flooded quarry: Sable, a soldier who erased his own name, twin oracles who see only endings, and old Maren, a hedge-witch who once taught Kestrel's mentor. They swear an oath to reach the Door together. Emotional beat: belonging found among the hunted.

chapters.title: Dain's Mercy
chapters.summary: Dain's POV. Dain captures one of the twins and offers Kestrel pardon in a letter: come home, renounce the gift, be a boy again. Kestrel wavers, tempted by the self he might have been. Emotional beat: the seduction of surrender — power's price versus identity's comfort.

chapters.title: The Price of the Ferry
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. To cross the drowned river, Maren spends her magic to still the water and dies of it, smiling. The group learns the Door demands a greater payment than any coin: a self, given wholly. Emotional beat: grief that hardens into resolve, and the first true understanding of the cost.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Eaten from the Edges
chapters.summary: Soldier's POV. The land itself is failing — roads loop, villages unremember, the stars shift. The soldier confesses he sold names to the crown to survive, and the group nearly turns on him. Kestrel stops the violence with magic he can no longer suppress. Emotional beat: survival's compromises exposed; the band fractures and reforges.

chapters.title: The Hollow Door
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. They find the Door: a standing stone in a field of ungrass, humming with everything the country has forgotten. It will open — but only for a self freely given. Dain arrives with the hunt, and Kestrel faces him across the stones. Emotional beat: confrontation where old love and new duty collide.

chapters.title: An Oath for the Hollow
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, climax. Dain offers one last pardon; Kestrel refuses and speaks his oath, pouring his name, gift, and memory into the Door. It opens in fire and silence. Dain, broken by recognition of the boy he was hunting, lets the fugitives pass instead of firing. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice as both ruin and triumph.

chapters.title: The Land That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, resolution. Beyond the border, the survivors are safe and nameless, carrying Kestrel nowhere in their memories — yet Sable plants a garden in a new valley and feels an old magic in the soil, gentle, watchful. The country that no longer exists keeps its keeper. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into quiet, living tribute.
